skill.name: scientific-schematics
skill.description: Create publication-quality scientific schematics from natural language prompts. The skill uses OpenRouter image models, Gemini-based review, document-type quality thresholds, versioned image outputs, and review logs for scientific figures.
skill.summary: Generate AI scientific schematics with quality review and versioned outputs.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection attempts were found in the reviewed files. Most static alerts are Markdown formatting, documentation URLs, placeholders, or test-only environment handling. Confirmed issues involve outbound OpenRouter calls, command-line API key exposure, broad .env loading, persistent secret storage examples, and user-directed file writes.

remediation.issue: API keys can be passed through command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Remove --api-key forwarding and read secrets only from environment variables or an explicit secure config path.

remediation.issue: The dotenv loader searches parent directories.
remediation.suggestion: Load only an explicit .env path or the project-local .env file, and document expected permissions and .gitignore rules.

remediation.issue: Documentation recommends persistent secret storage and echoing keys.
remediation.suggestion: Replace ~/.bashrc, echo, and inline-key examples with safer environment setup guidance that does not display the secret.

remediation.issue: Prompts and images are sent to a third-party API.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy notice and advise users not to submit confidential research data without approval.
Warn before overwriting files and consider restricting generated outputs to a configured figures directory.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Exposure Through Command-Line Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The wrapper forwards the OpenRouter API key using --api-key, and the implementation exposes a command-line key option. Secrets in process arguments can be visible to local users, shell history, or logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly appends the API key to argv and defines a CLI flag for the same secret. This is a well-known credential exposure pattern even without command injection.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Disclosure of Prompts and Images
semantic_findings.description: The generator sends user prompts to the image model and sends generated images with review prompts to a third-party API. Users could unintentionally disclose unpublished diagrams, study details, or confidential designs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The request payloads include the user prompt and review image data, and requests.post sends them to the configured OpenRouter endpoint. This is intended behavior but creates a clear privacy dependency.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Parent Directory Dotenv Loading
semantic_findings.description: The dotenv loader searches the working directory and multiple parent directories for .env files. This can import credentials from unrelated projects instead of requiring an explicit secret location.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The loop walks parent directories and loads the first .env it finds. The behavior is visible in code, but impact depends on where users run the script.

high_findings.title: Hidden file in home directory
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation tells users to append API keys to shell startup files under the home directory. This persists secrets in hidden files and can expose them through dotfile sharing or backups.

content.value_statement: Scientific diagrams are slow to draft and hard to polish for publication. This skill generates AI diagrams, reviews quality, and saves versioned outputs.
actual_capabilities: Generates PNG scientific diagrams from natural language prompts through OpenRouter image models.
Reviews generated images with Gemini and scores them against document-specific quality thresholds.
Saves versioned iteration images and a review log beside the final image.
Supports document types such as journal, conference, poster, presentation, grant, thesis, and preprint.
Provides prompt guidance for flowcharts, neural networks, pathways, circuits, and system architecture diagrams.
Includes dry-run tests for imports, class structure, error handling, and prompt construction.
limitations: Requires an OpenRouter API key and internet access.
Generated diagrams still need expert review for scientific accuracy and text fidelity.
Outputs raster images, so some journals may still require vector source files.
Review logs can include user prompts and generated image paths.

use_cases.title: Create Manuscript Figures
use_cases.description: Generate CONSORT, PRISMA, pathway, or method diagrams with review scores for publication drafts.

use_cases.title: Document Model Architectures
use_cases.description: Turn neural network or system descriptions into labeled architecture diagrams for papers and presentations.

use_cases.title: Prepare Grant Visuals
use_cases.description: Create clear workflow and conceptual diagrams for proposals, posters, and technical reports.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Simple Figure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a basic diagram.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a clean scientific diagram for this topic: [topic]. Use clear labels, simple layout, and high contrast.

prompt_templates.title: Specify Layout and Labels
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with structure and annotations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [diagram type] with [main components]. Arrange it [left to right or top to bottom]. Label each connection with [labels].

prompt_templates.title: Target a Publication Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using document-specific quality thresholds.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a [journal or poster] quality figure showing [process]. Include required labels, units, legend details, and colorblind-safe colors.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Complex Schematic
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for dense scientific systems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a publication-ready schematic for [complex system]. Include components, flow direction, quantitative values, visual hierarchy, and accessibility requirements.

output_examples.input: Create a CONSORT flow diagram with screened, excluded, randomized, follow-up, and analyzed participant counts.
output_examples.output: A versioned set of flowchart images with labeled study stages, participant counts, and a quality review summary.

output_examples.input: Create a transformer encoder-decoder architecture with attention blocks and cross-attention links.
output_examples.output: A labeled architecture diagram with separate encoder and decoder sections, connection arrows, and review feedback.

output_examples.input: Create a MAPK pathway from EGFR to gene transcription with phosphorylation labels.
output_examples.output: A biological pathway schematic with protein steps, activation arrows, membrane context, and accessibility-focused colors.

best_practices: Describe the exact diagram type, components, flow direction, and labels before generating.
Use document type settings so quality thresholds match the intended venue.
Review the final image, review log, and scientific accuracy before publication.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague prompts such as make a diagram.
Do not paste confidential unpublished data unless third-party API use is approved.
Do not assume generated labels, counts, or pathway relationships are scientifically correct without review.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires an OpenRouter API key for image generation and review calls.

faq.question: Can it create publication-ready figures?
faq.answer: It targets publication quality, but users must still verify scientific accuracy and journal format requirements.

faq.question: What file types does it create?
faq.answer: The implementation writes PNG images and a review log for the generation process.

faq.question: Does it support different document types?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes quality thresholds for journals, conferences, posters, presentations, reports, grants, theses, and preprints.

faq.question: Are prompts sent to a third-party service?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts and image review inputs are sent to OpenRouter-backed models for generation and evaluation.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
